case.label: B
case.text: B also restores the calls: an allow-all outbound rule on the service subnet's network ACL lets the responses leave, which is what the REJECT records point to. It loses only on the MOST secure qualifier, because it opens every port to every destination where D opens only the ephemeral range to the client CIDR. A fails because the client subnet's default network ACL already allows all inbound traffic, and C fails because security groups are stateful, so a service-side outbound rule has no effect on responses. The stem states the qualifier, the default network ACL on the client side and the Amazon Linux client OS (which fixes the 32768-61000 range), so no second answer stays defensible; the only cue is that 'flow log for the service' with REJECT on responses points directly at the service subnet's outbound network ACL rules, which is the intended reasoning, not a giveaway.
